title: Make Athena's deterministic plan findings not count as planning rounds
summary: Findings from Athena's own plan rules (plan_findings, no critic call) go back to the planner for an immediate revision that does not use a planning round, up to two such passes per round; only critic reviews count toward max_rounds. Audience: maintainers and the job pipeline, whose hard jobs lose critic rounds to mechanical findings.

defaults_applied.how: Change and tests are Rust in athena-core.
New tests plus fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test criteria.
Criteria check the planner re-invocation and critic round numbering by test, not wiring.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Fixes the round accounting rather than raising max_rounds.
One focused change in the planning loop.
The two-pass cap is enforced in code and tested.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs (plan_round loops rounds 1..=max_rounds; planning_round runs the planner, then plan_findings, and on a Blocker/Major finding calls end_round with a Revise critique and no critic call, consuming the round) and grep of crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (existing planning tests, plan_verdict at ~210, plan_round call at ~892). The loop change lands in planning.rs though the request names only mod.rs; tests go in mod.rs.

Plan records and critiques are keyed by job and round; the mechanical pass must not collide with the critic's round numbering (e.g. mechanical plans are not filed as records, or are filed without a critique, but the final stop must still record the finding). The producer must check how closing.plans/critiques are validated and persisted; records validation allow-list is unchanged because no new record or data file is added.

The two-pass cap applies per critic round (each critic round gets up to two mechanical passes); a plan still breaking a rule after two passes stops planning with that finding. If this should be a job-wide cap instead, that is a small change.
Mechanical passes need planner budget; the existing check_budget before each planner call applies, and a budget stop ends planning as today.
No new refusal reading rule is added to readings; this changes planning flow, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not changed; max_rounds config semantics stay the same.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs uses a fake planner whose first plan breaks a deterministic plan rule (e.g. missing fails_without); run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the planner is invoked again with the finding, the critic is first called on the fixed plan labelled round 1, and no critic call precedes it.

A test with max_rounds = 3 shows that after one mechanical revision the critic can still review in rounds 1, 2 and 3 (three critic calls) before the cap stops the job; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A test shows a plan that still breaks a rule after two mechanical passes stops planning (job failed with the planning-stopped prefix) with that finding in the reason, and the critic is never called; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

The planning loop in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs no longer ends a round on Blocker/Major plan_findings by consuming a round; the cap of two mechanical passes is a named constant or documented, and the plan_round doc comment states that only critic reviews count toward max_rounds.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that deterministic plan-rule findings are revised without using a planning round or a critic call, at most twice.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
Existing planning tests (soundness findings, revise in last round, resume with seed revision) still pass unchanged in behavior; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

out_of_scope: Changing max_rounds defaults or [job_plan] values in athena.toml
Changing what the plan rules or the critic flag
Changing the planner or critic prompts
departures: Hard job touching the planning pipeline with round accounting and record keying, so higher cost and time than the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: mechanical plan findings burn planning rounds and stop hard jobs at the cap, causing failed attempts.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline's planning loop (how a job's plan is revised, reviewed and stopped), so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
